content.text: Section 20 satisfies every preferred element, and indemnity obligations are Excluded Claims (uncapped), which is better than the fallback super-cap.

input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position in full. 20.1 gives an express Vendor duty to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel against third-party claims that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate IP. 20.2 extends the same defence and indemnity to Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. 20.4 supplies the standard procedure — prompt notice, reasonable cooperation (at the indemnifying Party's expense) and control of the defence — with a settlement-consent protection favouring the indemnified party. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is properly narrow: only unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, plus Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with carve-backs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. Beyond the preferred checklist, 20.5 adds the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder (cross-referenced by the 9.3 termination right), and 21.3 treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims, so Vendor's indemnity is uncapped rather than subject to the fallback 3× super-cap. No redline is warranted.
